summary.statement: Small and mid-size contractors assign COI collection, expiry tracking and contract-compliance checks to project coordinators/administrators.
Tracking is done in spreadsheets, PDFs and inboxes, or in a construction ERP with manually entered COI dates.
Smaller firms often stay on spreadsheets rather than buy enterprise tools; a spreadsheet is seen as adequate for very small sub counts.
COI work is one duty of $55k-60k/year coordinator roles; no posting isolates how many hours it takes.
Vendor estimates range from ~15 hours/year of data entry at 45 subs to 8-12 hours/week; these are unsourced vendor claims.
A missing sub COI at workers' comp premium audit can add that sub's full cost to the contractor's payroll base.
In the evidence, the people engaging on COI process are finance roles (a Controller asking peers on CFMA; coordinators reporting to PM and Controller).
No evidence found showing who signs off on purchasing COI software at a small GC.
Dedicated tools exist at every price point: enterprise (CertFocus, myCOI, Jones), freemium (bcs free to 25 vendors, TrustLayer free under 50) and indie $29-49/month tools.
Some GCs use their ERP (CMiC) or generic AI extraction into a spreadsheet instead of a dedicated tool.
Brokers bear unpaid COI workload and resent contractor systems that make them upload (one charged agents $15 per upload).
Competitors claim login requirements reduce vendor submission rates, but this is unquantified vendor marketing.
No-login submission links already exist at bcs, Billy and Jones, and one source says vendors want an upload link rather than emailing PDFs.
Email-only chasing is also painful: one property manager describes 3-week email chains per certificate.
Incumbent minimums are real: CertFocus $7,500 self-service / $10,000 full-service plus implementation; bcs full-service $10,000.
But self-serve pricing far below $99/month already exists: bcs at $0.95/vendor/month, TrustLayer free under 50 vendors, indie tools at $29-49/month.
No evidence found of what small GCs currently budget for COI tooling.
Workers' comp premium audits, claims and loss-control inspections are when subcontractor COIs get demanded.
Claims where the GC lacked an actual additional-insured endorsement have left GCs uncovered (a 2026 Arkansas case exceeding $1.2M; a California scaffolding case).
Mid-project expirations and owner/audit requests for proof also trigger reviews (vendor framing).

new_unknowns.question: Would small GCs pay $99/month when bcs (free to 25 vendors, then $0.95/vendor/month) and TrustLayer (free under 50) already exist?
Does endorsement-level parsing (AI/waiver language on attached CG 20 10/20 37 pages) measurably beat bcs/Billy/Jones accuracy?

current_solutions.statement: Coordinators at small GCs track COIs in spreadsheets, shared folders and email, or key COI dates into a construction ERP such as CMiC.
Firms that buy software choose between sales-led incumbents with $7,500-$10,000 minimums and self-serve tools that are free at low vendor counts (bcs, TrustLayer).
A wave of indie tools (CertKeeper, COIPulse, VendorShield, CertTrack Lite) already targets the sub-$100/month small-contractor segment, one with the same no-portal pitch.
Outsourced full-service review is available but carries $10,000 annual minimums.
